rubrics.justification: Accurately describes a good-quality blastocyst with strong ICM and looser B-grade TE, and appropriately notes uncertainty between stage 3 and early 4; minor limitation is reliance on image details not fully verifiable from a single static view.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, smoking, prior IVF outcomes, male factor diagnosis, sperm parameters, endometrial thickness, and transfer timing into prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with probability estimate tied to embryo quality and patient factors; slight overemphasis on some lifestyle factors and the 3AB vs 4AB discrepancy keeps it from perfect.

Generally aligns well with Gardner grading, eSET preference in a young patient, caution about PGT-A at age 28, and avoiding bed rest; minor deviations include somewhat assertive interpretation of smoking/BMI effects on implantation magnitude.

Provides clear, practical recommendations for current transfer and future planning, including eSET, smoking cessation, luteal support adherence, prenatal optimization, and targeted evaluation if future failures occur.
